idiom_name: first-class function argument (Node error-first callback) and listener registration
implementation_notes: Functions are values, so the classic structure disappears: the callback is simply an argument, and what remains are conventions - Node's error-first (err, result) completion and DOM-style listener registration through EventTarget. Modern code replaces chains of nested callbacks with promises and async/await (util.promisify converts a callback API, util.callbackify goes the other way), which is the reason to prefer a callback only where it is the native shape: event handlers (addEventListener), APIs that may invoke the callback zero or many times (streams, progress), and Node's historical I/O surface. A callback that must survive sequences of steps is a code smell in JavaScript, not a design.
pitfalls: Registration and removal must use the same function reference; an inline arrow passed to addEventListener or removeListener can never be removed.
A throw inside a callback invoked from the event loop (timer, I/O completion) surfaces as an uncaughtException or an unhandled rejection instead of travelling back to the initiating call.
A method passed as a callback loses its receiver (this is undefined in strict mode); bind it or wrap it in an arrow function.
Calling back synchronously on some paths and asynchronously on others (zalgo) exposes two orders to callers; defer with process.nextTick or queueMicrotask.
